title: Ibrahim at the House
hookLine: make this city safe, and make me and my offspring keep up prayer (14:35–41)
last: A GOOD WORD IS A TREE.

lines: THE VALLEY, FROM THE FATHER'S SIDE.
cards: You met Hajar in the valley months ago, near the start of this path: a mother, a baby, a water skin, and a man walking away who said God had commanded it.
Surah Ibrahim goes back to that valley from the other side, the father's. It keeps his prayer, line by line.
A long report in Bukhari has him saying part of it as he walked away that day; the prayer also thanks God for two sons given in old age, so commentators differ over when each line was said.
Either way, you overhear a father's whole list of requests.

teach.b: Listen to what he asks for, in order. First: my Lord, make this city safe. Not rich, not well-known.
Safe. Then: keep me and my sons from worshiping idols; they have led many people astray.
Then, in verse thirty-seven, in paraphrase: our Lord, I have settled some of my children in a valley with no crops, by Your sacred House, so that they may keep up the prayer.

So make the hearts of people yearn toward them, and provide them with fruits, so that they may be grateful. He doesn't ask for fruit first. He asks for hearts: people's hearts, turning toward a valley with no crops.
Then he thanks God for giving him Isma'il and Ishaq in his old age.

teach.h: MAKE ME KEEP UP THE PRAYER.
teach.b: And then the line in Pickthall's translation: "My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also); our Lord! and accept the prayer."

And last: our Lord, forgive me, and my parents, and the believers, on the day the reckoning is set up. Some Muslims recite those last two verses near the end of their own prayer, just before the closing greetings.
So a father's words at the House come back inside the prayer of people who face that same valley.
He asked that his children would keep the prayer, and his words are said in it.

how: Some Muslims recite Ibrahim's words from 14:40–41, rabbi j'alni muqima s-salati, in the final sitting of the daily prayer before the closing salam, and parents often say them for their children.

o: the prophet whose prayer asks for a safe city
the son left as a baby in the valley
the prophet who led his people out of Egypt

p: make people's hearts yearn toward them
forgive me, my parents, the believers

s: Ibrahim asks first for the city to be rich
he asks first for it to be safe.
Ibrahim asks for people's hearts before he asks for fruit
make hearts yearn toward them, and provide them with fruits.
Muslims still recite Ibrahim's words in the daily prayer
some say 14:40–41 in the last sitting, before the closing greetings.

games.q: you're Ibrahim, old, at the House in a valley with no crops. you can ask God for one thing first. what does he ask?
games.why: make this city safe. then: keep us from idols, make hearts yearn toward them, and make me and my children keep up the prayer.

practice: Bring to mind the children in your life: your own, ones you hope for, nieces, nephews, students, the kids next door, and picture their faces.
What would you ask for them, if you made a list like Ibrahim's: safety, good hearts around them, a practice that holds them?
If you pray, recite Ibrahim's words or ask in your own language; if not, simply hold them in mind with care.

wordCard.voice: Ibrahim. The old father's prayer at the sacred House: a safe city, hearts that yearn, and children who keep up the prayer. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "my Lord, make me one who keeps up the prayer" (14:40).

carryVoice: Your line: make us keep the prayer. A father's list, still being said. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also); our Lord! and accept the prayer.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3364 (Hajar and the infant in the valley; Ibrahim's prayer as he leaves)
